title: NISM Research Analyst (Series XV)
blurb: Exam prep for NISM-Series-XV: SEBI RA rules, conduct, economy, industry, company analysis, valuation, technicals and report writing.

rows: Anyone who writes, reviews or publishes research, and RAs preparing for NISM-Series-XV
About 110 minutes of lessons, then cards, checkpoints and the final quiz
None. Basic comfort with percentages and financial statements helps
18 short lessons in 6 stages, each ending with three exam-style checks
outcomes: Explain who needs SEBI research analyst registration and what the regulations require.
Apply the conduct, disclosure and trading-restriction rules to real situations.
Read macro data, industry structure and financial statements to form a view.
Value a company with DCF and relative multiples and state the assumptions.
Write a research report with rating, target price, risks and the mandatory disclosures.

sources: SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, 2014 and later amendments and circulars (check the current text)
NISM-Series-XV: Research Analyst Certification Examination workbook (current edition)
SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015; SEBI PFUTP Regulations, 2003
RBI monetary policy framework; MoSPI release calendar for GDP and CPI
Practice exam only: confirm the current NISM exam format, marks and pass mark before booking

final.title: NISM Research Analyst (Series XV) final quiz

questions.q: A recommendation with a target price on a stock, given to the public, is:
o: Research that needs a registered RA
Only a tip if it is free
questions.why: Recommendations and target prices fall under the RA regulations whatever the channel.

questions.q: A research report is best described as:
o: Analysis of securities with a recommendation, rating or target price
questions.why: The defining feature is the recommendation, rating or target price.

questions.q: Shares sold by one investor to another on an exchange are traded in the:
questions.why: Secondary markets trade existing securities; the issuer gets no proceeds.

questions.q: Which form of efficiency says all public information is already in the price?
questions.why: Semi-strong: public information is reflected; strong adds private information.

questions.q: Which certification is expected of a research analyst?
questions.why: NISM-Series-XV is the research analyst certification.

questions.q: Records of research and rationale should be kept for at least:
questions.why: The regulations require a minimum five-year record.

questions.q: Trading ahead of a published recommendation is called:
questions.why: Front running exploits knowledge of an upcoming recommendation.

questions.q: A report must disclose analyst or relatives' holdings of at least:
questions.why: A holding of 1% or more must be disclosed.

questions.q: Personalised, fee-only advice to a client needs registration as a(n):
questions.why: Personalised advice falls under the Investment Advisers regulations.

questions.q: Fees for RA services must be:
questions.why: Fees are disclosed and charged directly.

questions.q: The policy rate at which RBI lends to banks is the:
questions.why: Repo is the key short-term lending rate.

questions.q: A weaker rupee typically benefits:
questions.why: Exporters earn in foreign currency, so a weaker rupee lifts rupee revenue.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of Porter's five forces?
questions.why: Dividend yield is a valuation metric, not a force.

questions.q: Which sector is typically defensive?
questions.why: FMCG demand is stable through cycles.

questions.q: EBITDA minus depreciation is:
questions.why: EBIT = EBITDA − depreciation and amortisation.

questions.q: Free cash flow is typically:
questions.why: FCF = operating cash flow less capital expenditure.

questions.q: DuPont ROE equals:
questions.why: ROE is the product of margin, asset turnover and leverage.

questions.q: Interest coverage is calculated as:
questions.why: Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest expense.

questions.q: CFO persistently far below PAT suggests:
questions.why: Profit not converting to cash is a classic warning sign.

questions.q: Receivables growing much faster than sales may indicate:
questions.why: It can signal stretched credit terms or early revenue booking.

questions.q: In the Gordon growth model, terminal value equals:
questions.why: TV = FCF₁ ÷ (WACC − g).

questions.q: CAPM cost of equity is:
questions.why: Cost of equity = risk-free rate + beta × market risk premium.

questions.q: Enterprise value equals:
questions.why: EV = market cap + debt − cash (and minorities).

questions.q: Which multiple suits banks best?
questions.why: For lenders, book value and returns on equity matter most.

questions.q: An RSI above 70 is usually read as:
questions.why: RSI over 70 suggests the move may be stretched.

questions.q: A 'golden cross' is when:
questions.why: The short average crossing above the long one is a bullish signal.

questions.q: The maximum loss for an option buyer is:
questions.why: A buyer can lose only the premium.

questions.q: A research report should always state:
o: Rating, target price and horizon with risks
questions.why: Rating, target price, horizon and risks give the reader the full picture.

questions.q: UPSI stands for:
questions.why: UPSI is non-public information that could move a price.

questions.q: Giving a preview of a report only to some clients is:
questions.why: All clients should receive research at the same time.

questions.q: A good worked review should connect:
o: Macro, industry, company, valuation and conduct
questions.why: Strong research builds from the top down and ends with conduct checks.
